citation: Ryan 2013, Impact of an anti-idling campaign on outdoor air quality at four urban schools
evidence: After the anti-idling campaign the school-minus-community PM2.5 difference at the school with the most buses (n=39) fell from 4.11 to 0.99 ug/m3 (p<0.05), while schools with 5 to 11 buses showed no significant change.

citation: Ryan 2013, Impact of an anti-idling campaign on outdoor air quality at four urban schools
evidence: At the school with the most buses, the school-minus-community particle number concentration fell from 11,560 to 1,690 particles/cm3 after the campaign (p<0.05).

citation: Ryan 2013, Impact of an anti-idling campaign on outdoor air quality at four urban schools
evidence: The school-minus-community elemental carbon difference fell from 0.40 to 0.15 ug/m3 at the school with the most buses after the anti-idling campaign.

citation: Mendoza 2022, Air quality and behavioral impacts of anti-idling campaigns in school drop-off zones
evidence: Two anti-idling campaigns in Salt Lake County produced a 38% decrease in idling time and an 11% decrease in the number of vehicles idling at school drop-off zones, with air quality improvement mid-campaign masked by seasonal variability and inversions.

citation: Gulf News, Leaving your vehicle engine running while idle incurs Dh300 fine (Abu Dhabi Police)
evidence: Abu Dhabi Police fine motorists Dh300 for leaving the engine running unattended at ATMs, shops or fuel stations, with theft and child safety as the stated reasons and no air quality rationale, so the UAE rule exists but is not enforced as an emissions measure.

citation: Tong 2025, Further improvement in London's air quality demands more than the ULEZ
evidence: Weather-normalised NO2 at central London traffic sites fell 19.6% (about 13.3 ug/m3) three months after ULEZ1 and 17.8% after 11 months, with 6.6% at urban background sites, while the 2023 expansion produced no statistically significant NO2 change.

citation: Tong 2025, Further improvement in London's air quality demands more than the ULEZ
evidence: The impact of ULEZ1 on PM2.5 was limited, with only central London traffic sites showing a 12.7% reduction (about 1.8 ug/m3) after three months and no significant change at background sites.

citation: Tong 2025, Further improvement in London's air quality demands more than the ULEZ
evidence: Before ULEZ1 around 39% of vehicles (about 35,578) entering central London were non-compliant with Euro 4 petrol and Euro 6 diesel standards, and NOx at central traffic sites fell 28.8% (about 48.1 ug/m3) three months after ULEZ1, while after the 2023 expansion non-compliant vehicles fell only 2.7 to 4.7% with no detectable NOx change.

citation: Simona 2025, Classroom air quality in a randomized crossover trial with portable HEPA air cleaners
evidence: In HEPA classrooms average school-year PM2.5 was 39.9% lower (0.581 ug/m3, p<0.001) than non-HEPA classrooms.

citation: Simona 2025, Classroom air quality in a randomized crossover trial with portable HEPA air cleaners
evidence: Infiltration of outdoor PM2.5 into classrooms was 13.8% to 82.4% lower in HEPA classrooms than non-HEPA classrooms, depending on the school.

citation: O'Driscoll 2018, Real world CO2 and NOx emissions from 149 Euro 5 and 6 passenger cars
evidence: PEMS tests of 149 cars found gasoline vehicles emitted 86 to 96% less NOx than diesel and Euro 6 diesel urban NOx averaged 0.44 g/km, 11 times the gasoline 0.04 g/km, so the authors call discrimination by Euro standard alone arbitrary and favour real-world limits.

citation: GSO 2025, Workshop on the implementation of new vehicle emission limits in the UAE
evidence: From 1 January 2026 new models of light and heavy vehicles imported to the UAE must meet at least Euro 6B, from 1 July 2027 all imports must, with 10 ppm sulphur fuel under UAE.S 477:2021 and UAE.S 5018:2021, and Euro 6D or Euro VI/D real driving emissions from 2030 model year.

citation: GSO 2025, Workshop on the implementation of new vehicle emission limits in the UAE
evidence: The UAE Euro 6B requirement applies gaseous pollutant plus PM plus particle number limits (PN 6x10^11 per km) to petrol and diesel light vehicles and Euro VI/B limits to heavy vehicles.

citation: Crippa 2016, Forty years of improvements in European air quality
evidence: The EURO norms for vehicles led to a 50% reduction of PM2.5 from global road transport exhaust emissions, and fuel sulphur directives to an 88% reduction of road SO2, with the increase in energy consumption 1970 to 2010 offsetting 40 to 75% of the gains.

citation: Eckel 2026, Zero-emissions vehicle adoption and satellite-measured NO2 in California 2019 to 2023
evidence: A within-ZIP-area increase of 200 zero-emission vehicles was associated with a 1.10% (95% CI 1.00 to 1.19) decrease in annual mean TROPOMI NO2, replicated at 0.87% with ground monitors.

citation: Eckel 2026, Zero-emissions vehicle adoption and satellite-measured NO2 in California 2019 to 2023
evidence: The positive control showed a 0.80% increase in annual NO2 per 800 additional internal combustion vehicles while 200 additional ZEVs gave a 1.10% decrease, which the authors attribute to reduced exhaust emissions.

citation: Hicks 2023, Quantifying the change of brake wear PM emissions through powertrain electrification
evidence: Regenerative braking would reduce brake wear by 64 to 95% despite heavier vehicles, an average 68% cut in urban brake wear PM emission factors, but increases in tyre wear, road wear and resuspension from higher vehicle mass may offset these benefits.

citation: ENEC 2026, The Barakah Plant and Climate Change

citation: MOCCAE 2022, UAE National Air Quality Agenda 2031

citation: Abu Dhabi DoE 2024, Abu Dhabi Energy and Water Efficiency Strategy 2030 (DSM strategy)

citation: Abu Dhabi DoE 2024, Abu Dhabi Energy and Water Efficiency Strategy 2030 (DSM strategy)
evidence: The electricity and water savings achieved up to 2023 avoided the emission of approximately 4.3 million tonnes of CO2.

citation: Climate Policy Database, Estidama Pearl Rating System for new residential and commercial buildings
evidence: Abu Dhabi made the Estidama Pearl Rating mandatory for new residential and commercial buildings in 2010, and the minimum standard Pearl 1 improves building efficiency by 30 to 35% versus the existing baseline.

citation: Ham 2024, Particulate matter reduction efficiency of sprinkler systems for construction activity
evidence: In a dust chamber during block cutting, water spraying at 115 bar achieved 95% PM reduction and 80 to 100 bar achieved 83%, while dust suppressant reached 83% at 100 bar and about 70% at 80 bar.

citation: Kumar 2024, Air pollution abatement from green-blue-grey infrastructure
evidence: Across 22 GBGI types with quantitative data the average pollution reduction was 16 plus or minus 21%, with linear features such as street trees and hedges at 23 plus or minus 21%, NOx reduced 12 plus or minus 36%, UFP 27 plus or minus 27%, BC 16 plus or minus 41% and PM2.5 only 1 plus or minus 25%.

citation: Kumar 2024, Air pollution abatement from green-blue-grey infrastructure
evidence: Street trees generally showed adverse effects in street canyons and beneficial outcomes in open-road conditions.

citation: Matthaios 2024, Effects of urban green space and road proximity on indoor traffic-related PM2.5 NO2 and BC in inner-city schools
evidence: Across 74 schools over 10 years, greenness (NDVI) within 270 m was associated with lower indoor traffic-related PM2.5 (-0.068, 95% CI -0.124 to -0.013), NO2 (-0.139, 95% CI -0.185 to -0.092) and BC (-0.060, 95% CI -0.115 to -0.005).

citation: Matthaios 2024, Effects of urban green space and road proximity on indoor traffic-related PM2.5 NO2 and BC in inner-city schools
evidence: Indoor traffic-related PM2.5, NO2 and BC showed linear decays of 60%, 35% and 22% respectively for schools located at greater distance from major roads.

citation: Mayor of London 2021, School Streets Air Quality Study
evidence: Breathe London sensors (30 sensors at 18 primary schools in Brent, Enfield and Lambeth) found closing roads around schools at pick-up and drop-off reduced nitrogen dioxide by up to 23%.

citation: TfL 2021, School Streets reduce nitrogen dioxide by up to 23% during morning drop-off (Local Transport Today)

citation: Simeonova 2019, Congestion pricing, air pollution and children's health (NBER w24410)
evidence: After the Stockholm congestion charge became permanent, NO2 fell 6.2 units and PM10 4.56 units, a 18.7% and 13.7% reduction relative to pre-charge means, with inner-city traffic down around 20 to 25%.

citation: Simeonova 2019, Congestion pricing, air pollution and children's health (NBER w24410)
evidence: The permanent congestion charge zone corresponded to a 13.7% reduction in PM10 relative to pre-charge Stockholm levels.

citation: Simeonova 2019, Congestion pricing, air pollution and children's health (NBER w24410)

evidence: Across 71 transit strikes in the five largest German cities 2002 to 2011, total car hours operated increased by 11 to 13% during strikes, so available transit holds car traffic down by that margin.

citation: Adar 2015, Adopting clean fuels and technologies on school buses: pollution and health impacts in children
evidence: Across 597 trips on 188 school buses, fine and ultrafine particle concentrations on board were 10 to 50% lower on buses using ultra-low-sulphur diesel, diesel oxidation catalysts or closed crankcase ventilation, and ULSD adoption cut absenteeism 8% (95% CI 0.7 to 16%).

citation: Bursey 2025, Health economic and environmental impacts of electric school bus adoption: scoping review

citation: Crippa 2016, Forty years of improvements in European air quality

citation: D'Antoni 2017, Predictors of adherence to health advice accompanying air quality warning systems: systematic review
evidence: Across 21 studies, actual adherence to advice to reduce or reschedule outdoor activity during poor air quality episodes ranged from 9.7% to 57% (median 31%), and adherence to wider protective behaviours ranged 17.7% to 98.1% (median 46%).

citation: MOCCAE 2022, UAE National Air Quality Agenda 2031
evidence: The Agenda lists as a gap that there is currently no system to warn the public about inevitable high-level pollution episodes such as dust storms and to provide guidance on how to reduce personal exposure.

citation: Sarani 2025, Mitigation strategies of healthcare centers for dust hazard: systematic review
evidence: Across 10 studies the most important mitigation measures were risk assessment, establishment and improvement of the early warning system, and intersectoral coordination, to reduce health consequences of dust storms in the affected community.

citation: Hlophe 2024, Interventions to reduce the impact of outdoor air pollution on asthma: systematic review
evidence: Mobile application alerts for outdoor smoke pollution produced behavioural change and improved Asthma Control Test scores over 8 weeks from 20.0 (SD 2.4) to 21.5 (SD 2.3), p<0.001, and clean air policy raised FEV1 by 0.01 L/year.
